# TRACE-0001: security traceability

<!-- Written by the security-requirements-auditor. Do not edit by hand. -->

Requirements: appsec-baseline `requirements/security-requirements.md` (working tree; commit SHA not available to the auditor; SR-031 assessed with the amended text in SPEC-0001 §9, because the file still carries the old wording until the amendment lands)
Artifacts reviewed: SPEC-0001.md (stage: spec, round 2; §11 normative) with INT-0001.md and reviews/INT-0001-status.md as context (working tree; commit SHA not available to the auditor)

## Triggers
| Trigger | True? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| INPUT | true | The verifier, `classify.py`, `hash.py`, `validate.py` and the gate parse review reports, file names, diffs, `/stage` arguments and reviewer output that come from PRs or agents (SPEC §2.1, §2.2, §2.5, M-15); SPEC §9 treats reports as untrusted input. |
| ENDPOINT | false | No HTTP endpoint or served page is added or changed; no change to the dogs-app API or UI (INT-0001 Visual: none). |
| WRITE | false | No caller creates, changes or deletes application data; the loop writes git artifacts only. |
| FILE | false | No file upload, storage or serving in the app; review reports are small git-tracked JSON files, not user file handling. |
| AUTHN | false | No change to how callers or operators are identified; the session keeps the owner's existing GitHub login (SPEC §4, owner decision 2026-10-28; issue #12 parked). |
| AUTHZ | true | SPEC §5 defines an authorisation matrix for owner, main session, subagents and CI, enforced by hook, permission rules and GitHub. |
| CRYPTO | true | SHA-256 over file contents binds reports to files (SPEC §2.2, §9 SR-021, M-05). |
| DATA | true | Artifacts, reports, exceptions, logs and session content are stored and transmitted; SPEC §6 inventories them (no personal data claimed). |
| LOG | true | SPEC §7 adds JSON Lines events from hook, gate, loop and verifier, plus job logs and summaries. |
| SECRET | true | CI uses `GITHUB_TOKEN`; the session holds the owner's login; federation rules, service accounts and variables are removed (SPEC §4, §8, M-10). |
| DEP | true | New scripts, a reusable workflow, pinned tools and the appsec-baseline lock (SPEC §2.1, §2.5, §2.6). |
| IAC | true | lab-admin `github.tf` changes (required checks, variables, labels, allowlist; SPEC §8). No AWS or IAM change. |
| CI | true | New `verify.yml`, `security.yml` changes, `security-gate`, `deploy.yml` job removed (SPEC §2.5-2.7, §8). |
| AI | true | The change adds the local agent loop, agent tools, models and gate (SPEC §1, §2.3, §11 M-17). |

## Summary
Covered: 13 · Missing: 0 · N/A: 18

Round 1: AUD-001 to AUD-012 resolved. Round 2: 8 new findings (AUD-001 to AUD-008 below, renumbered), none blocking: 5 medium, 3 low.

findings.evidence: §7 lists the fields `ts`, `level`, `event`, `outcome`, `actor`, `change`, `stage`, `request_id` and a never-logged list of 'tokens, `Authorization` headers, credentials, presigned URLs, full file contents, full reviewer output'. SR-024 also mandates `service`, `version`, `reason` (and `source_ip`, `http`, `resource` where applicable) and never logging Cookie headers, request or response bodies, email addresses and names. The spec does not say which fields are not applicable to non-HTTP events.
findings.recommendation: Add `service` and `version` (git SHA) to the field list, state that `source_ip`, `http` and `resource` are not applicable (no HTTP requests), add `reason` as a machine code, and extend the never-logged list with cookies, bodies, email addresses and names.

findings.evidence: §5 limits the author to 'only the current stage's artifact file; at the code stage only files listed in this repo's PLAN- section; never reviews/', but §10 names `test_hook_blocks_subagent_write_outside_change_folder`, which does not match that rule (the code stage writes outside the change folder). The CI column and the 'main session writes TRACE/THREAT only via write_artifact.py' cell have no named test in §10; §11 defers tests to THREAT-0001, which is not among the reviewed artifacts.
findings.recommendation: Add named tests for: author writing another stage's artifact or `reviews/` denied; code-stage author write limited to PLAN-listed files; main-session direct write of TRACE/THREAT denied; CI token cannot write beyond PR comments. Copy the M-xx test names into §10.

findings.evidence: M-07: 'the tests run in a separate job of `security.yml` with `contents: read` only, upload JUnit as an artifact'. No `timeout-minutes` is stated for this new job, while SR-030 requires one (at most 30) on every job; `verify` (15) and `security-gate` (5) have theirs.
findings.recommendation: State timeout-minutes (at most 30) for the named-tests job and that it needs no other permissions; cover it in the same actionlint or workflow-parse test as `security-gate`.

findings.evidence: §2.6 defines scanners only for dogs-app (`security.yml`). The new scripts (`validate.py`, `gate.py`, `hash.py`, `classify.py` and others) and the hashed lockfile for `jsonschema` and `PyYAML` live in appsec-baseline, whose workflows are `ci.yml` (gate tests only) and `security-review.yml`. No Semgrep, OSV-Scanner or gitleaks run on appsec-baseline PRs is specified.
findings.recommendation: State which job scans appsec-baseline PRs (Semgrep injection and TLS rules, OSV-Scanner on the lockfile, gitleaks) and add it to the appsec-baseline section of the plan, or record a time-boxed exception.

findings.evidence: M-15 gives the slug pattern `^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]{1,38}[a-z0-9])$`, which allows consecutive hyphens and has no word limit; §1.1 gives `^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$`, 3-40 characters, at most 5 words. §11 is normative, so the weaker pattern wins.
findings.recommendation: Use one pattern in both places, the stricter §1.1 form, and say which test checks it.

findings.evidence: M-05: 'TRACE-/THREAT- files are written by `write_artifact.py` from the validated `artifact` field'. §2.2 limits apply to the report, but no maximum length, UTF-8 or control-character rule is stated for the reviewer's `artifact` string, which is untrusted agent output written into the repo.
findings.recommendation: Give `artifact` a maximum length (for example 256 KiB), require valid UTF-8 without control characters other than newline and tab, and add it to the schema-rejection test.

findings.evidence: §6 data inventory lists artifacts, reports, exceptions, verifier logs and the stage log, but not the repo content and prompts the local session sends to the model provider, nor the Claude Code session transcripts kept on the owner's laptop.
findings.recommendation: Add two rows: content sent to the model provider (purpose, no personal data, provider retention) and local session transcripts (purpose, location, retention).

findings.evidence: §6: 'All stores are GitHub-managed (encrypted at rest by GitHub) or the owner's laptop'. SR-023 requires AES-256 at rest; the algorithm is not named for GitHub's stores and the laptop store (stage log) has no encryption statement.
findings.recommendation: Name the vendor encryption (AES-256 as documented by GitHub) or record it as a lab exception in BASELINE, and state that the laptop disk is encrypted (for example FileVault).
